what: Grayscale PDF removes the colour from a PDF, so it shows and prints in shades of grey or pure black and white. It is the easy way to save colour ink and to meet print-shop or office rules that ask for black-and-white files.

There are two ways to convert. "Keep text selectable" places a grey filter over every page: text stays real and sharp, links keep working, and the file stays small. "Rebuild pages as grey images" redraws each page as a grey picture, which truly removes every bit of colour data, but text can no longer be selected.
Both run in your browser with pdf-lib and PDF.js, and your file is never uploaded.
uses: Print documents with photos and coloured charts using only black ink.
Hand in a true greyscale file when colour printing costs extra.
Some teachers and exam boards ask for black-and-white documents.
Turn coloured scans into crisp pure black and white.
See whether charts and diagrams are still readable without colour.
tutorial: Click the box that says "Click or drop a PDF here", or drag the file onto it. The page count appears below.
"Keep text selectable (fast, small file)" or "Rebuild pages as grey images (strongest)". A note under the choice explains the difference.
Choose "Shades of grey" or "Pure black and white", and a quality from 150 to 300 dpi.
Click "Convert to greyscale". In rebuild mode the message counts the pages.
Small previews of the first pages appear so you can see the result.
Click "Download grey PDF". The file name ends in -grey.pdf.
features: A fast filter that keeps text, or a full rebuild that removes all colour data.
In the fast mode, text, links and vector drawings stay sharp and searchable.
Rebuild mode produces pages with no colour at all, ideal for print shops.
Turn scans and text into crisp pure black and white.
See the first pages before you download.

example.title: Worked example: a report for a print shop
example.text: Diego must print a 40-page report with coloured charts, and the print shop charges extra for colour. He chooses "Rebuild pages as grey images (strongest)", keeps "Shades of grey" and "High (200 dpi)", and clicks Convert to greyscale. The previews show grey charts, and he sends report-grey.pdf to the shop.

tips: For everyday printing at home, "Keep text selectable" is faster and keeps the file small.
For print shops that check colour, use "Rebuild pages as grey images".
Charts that use only colour to tell lines apart can become hard to read; check the preview.
Pure black and white works best for text and scans, not for photos.
problems: Highlights or form fields are still coloured
In the fast mode, comments and form fields stay on top in colour. Use the rebuild mode to flatten them.
Rebuild mode stores each page as a picture. Choose 150 dpi, or use the fast mode.
That is expected in rebuild mode. Use "Keep text selectable" if you need the text.
The message says the PDF is password protected
Remove the password with Unlock PDF first.
